title: It takes a village: Lady’s Choice leads a parent-kid-school partnership for healthier kids
summary: The Baon Buddies School Takeover brings families and educators together to make proper nutrition easier to practice every day

blocks.text: The Baon Buddies School Takeover brings families and educators together to make proper nutrition easier to practice every day

Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by Lady’s Choice Philippines and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

Raising healthy kids has never been the work of parents alone. Children move between different environments every day — from the breakfast table to the classroom, the school canteen, and the people they spend their day with. Each one can influence the habits they form around food and nutrition.

This means that while healthier choices may begin at home, they become easier to practice when the circles they move in reinforce them, too. Parents can prepare nutritious meals, and schools can reinforce nutrition education, but kids also need to understand the choices that keep them fueled throughout the day.

It is this shared responsibility that sits at the heart of Lady’s Choice’s 2026 Baon Buddies School Takeover, bringing parents, kids, and schools together to make proper nutrition something they can practice consistently wherever they are.
The campaign is built around a parent-kid-school partnership designed to support children’s nutrition beyond just the school day.

School takes up a lot of children’s time and energy. Between classes, playtime, and extracurricular activities, a school day can stretch beyond the hours spent sitting inside the classroom. Lady’s Choice’s campaign is rooted in the insight that meals and snacks should do more than simply fill children up; they should also help support them through the demands of the day.

That is why the Baon Buddies School Takeover brings the conversation on nutrition directly into schools. As part of the campaign, Lady’s Choice introduced its Baon Buddies, Sandy and Elsie, in school activations that make nutrition education more engaging for both parents and children. The program includes nutrition awareness explainers, sandwich-making workshops, an “Omega-sigla” quiz bee, and sandwich sampling.
Instead of treating healthy eating as another lesson children have to “learn”, the activities show that nutrition can be educational and enjoyable at the same time.

blocks.caption: SAMA SAMA SA NUTRISYON AT SIGLA. Kids in Upper Bicutan Elementary School participate in a sandwich making workshop.

blocks.text: For parents, baon can easily become another item on their morning agenda — but involving children in what goes into their lunchbox can also help turn food into a conversation. What do you like eating? What can we prepare for tomorrow? What gives you enough energy for the school day?
This kind of participation matters because healthy routines are easier to sustain when children understand and have a role in them.

The Lady’s Choice Baon Buddies campaign brings this conversation into schools through a nationwide roadshow as part of its effort to reach 70,000 school sampling hits. The roadshow is done in collaboration with the Department of Education in celebration of Nutrition Month, positioning schools not just as mere venues, but as partners in making nutrition awareness part of children’s learning.

blocks.caption: BAON BUDDIES. Making healthy eating more fun starts with meeting kids where they are.

blocks.text: Highlighted in Lady’s Choice’s back-to-school campaign are its Meaty Spreads, including chicken, ham, bacon, tuna, and plain variants, made with real meat and farm-fresh eggs that contain Omega-3 and 6 nutrients, as part of a proper diet and healthy lifestyle.

The campaign then brings these products into different parts of a child’s day — from breakfast, baon, and to merienda — through sandwich sampling, recipe videos, and digital content that give parents more ideas for preparing everyday meals and snacks.

Lady’s Choice taps into these different moments so healthy eating becomes something children can easily recognize. By showing how nutritious sandwiches and snacks can fit into different mealtimes, the campaign helps make better food choices feel easier to practice —supporting its larger goal of getting parents, kids, and schools to work together in building healthier everyday habits.
